model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of the LLM (Large Language Model) architecture, including “Vanilla,” “StrmLLM (n=64),” and multiple configurations of “SepLLM” with different sequence lengths (n=64 or n=128) and optional hierarchical or token-level adaptations (H, H/T). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 in linear scale with major gridlines and tick labels every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 in linear scale, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 0.1. All lines begin near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep initial decline before gradually converging toward lower loss values around 2.5 by iteration 140,000. The “Vanilla” model (purple, solid line) shows the smoothest descent and lowest final loss. “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid line) starts slightly lower than Vanilla but ends slightly higher. The “SepLLM (n=64)” variants (orange, green, red) follow similar trajectories, with “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red) performing slightly worse than “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green). The “SepLLM (n=128)” model (dark blue, solid line) starts higher than others and converges to a slightly higher loss than the n=64 variants, indicating that increasing sequence length may not improve convergence in this context. All lines exhibit small fluctuations, particularly in the early iterations, suggesting stochastic training dynamics.
